assessments.operationalization: Classify each bird species by the season containing most egg-laying records and test whether more than half peak in spring.

candidate_datasets.name: eBird
candidate_datasets.role: public bird observations that can support breeding-phenology estimates where breeding codes are available

obstacles: Spring differs between hemispheres.
Breeding observations are taxonomically and geographically biased.
assessments.rationale: The proposition has a clear seasonal test. Existing occurrence data can estimate breeding timing for many species, but do not directly and evenly record egg laying across birds worldwide.

assessments.operationalization: Compare clutch size distributions of raptors with other birds and test whether kestrels are an exception within raptors.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: species accounts containing clutch sizes for many raptors

obstacles: Unprolific requires a numerical threshold.
Coverage is incomplete across all birds of prey.
assessments.rationale: Clutch size is standard and readily compared, but the qualitative word unprolific needs an explicit reference group or cutoff. Public species accounts cover many, not all, relevant taxa.

assessments.operationalization: Measure shell hardness for fertilized eggs from healthy females across bird taxa and count exceptions to hard shells.
obstacles: No known open dataset combines shell hardness, fertilization, and maternal health.
The universal scope requires very broad taxonomic sampling.
assessments.rationale: The variables are measurable and a soft-shelled qualifying egg would refute the claim. Existing egg collections and papers are unlikely to encode all three required conditions at adequate scale.

assessments.operationalization: Compare yolk-to-albumen mass ratios between river or marsh birds and terrestrial birds while accounting for egg and adult size.
obstacles: Egg composition measurements are scattered.
Ecological categories require consistent assignment.
assessments.rationale: The comparison and decision criterion are direct. A broad public dataset of yolk and albumen masses across both ecological groups is not clearly available, so substantial compilation or new measurement would be needed.

assessments.operationalization: Observe or image egg orientation during oviposition and record whether the blunt end emerges first across species.
obstacles: Oviposition orientation is rarely included in trait databases.
The scope does not specify whether it applies to all birds.
assessments.rationale: Direct video observation would cleanly confirm or refute the statement. Existing public data appear anecdotal or species-specific rather than a reusable comparative dataset.

assessments.operationalization: Use husbandry records for unmated hens and geese to determine whether they lay eggs and verify that those eggs are unfertilized.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: public reproductive biology accounts for chickens and geese

obstacles: Detailed flock-level records may be reported in literature rather than one downloadable table.
assessments.rationale: Egg laying without mating is a standard, directly observable reproductive trait. Public veterinary and husbandry evidence is ample for the two named domestic birds and the test is simple.

assessments.operationalization: Compare days to hatch for naturally brooded chicken eggs in summer and winter and test the stated 18-day and up-to-25-day values.
obstacles: Modern incubation temperature is often controlled.
Season is confounded with temperature and husbandry.
assessments.rationale: Incubation duration is straightforward, but modern records often concern standardized artificial incubation rather than seasonal natural brooding. Existing evidence can test typical duration more readily than the precise seasonal contrast.

assessments.operationalization: Align the stated time with standard chicken embryo stages and determine whether the first visible embryo and beating heart occur after roughly 72 hours.
obstacles: The phrase first visible depends on imaging sensitivity.
assessments.rationale: Chicken development has detailed public staging resources. The timing and order of visible structures can be checked with standard embryological criteria, although visibility depends somewhat on method.

assessments.operationalization: At embryonic day 20, measure movement and vocalization after a standardized touch stimulus and compare with adjacent stages.
obstacles: Behavioral response data are not central variables in anatomical atlases.
Opening the egg changes the experimental condition.
assessments.rationale: The response and timing are measurable, and published incubation studies can address them. A public dataset directly pairing day, touch, movement, and chirping is less certain.

assessments.operationalization: Compile clutch sizes for pigeons, ringdoves, and turtle-doves and test whether two is the modal value and any clutch exceeds three.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: public species accounts with clutch-size information for pigeon-kind birds

obstacles: Common names must be mapped to species.
assessments.rationale: Clutch size is a standard life-history variable with broad public coverage. Both the modal value and the claimed upper bound yield explicit tests.

assessments.operationalization: Define body-size classes, compare incubation durations among them, and separately check geese, great bustards, kites, and hawks against 30- and 20-day values.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: species accounts containing incubation duration and body size

obstacles: Large and middle-sized are undefined.
Incubation varies substantially within size classes.
assessments.rationale: Named examples can be tested directly, while the general size-class relationship requires interpretive thresholds. Existing species data provide substantial but incomplete coverage.

assessments.operationalization: Check whether cuckoo species build nests, use host nests, and remove or consume host eggs before laying.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: public species accounts documenting cuckoo nesting and brood parasitism

obstacles: Behavior differs among cuckoo species.
The claim's singular cuckoo requires taxonomic mapping.
assessments.rationale: Nest building and brood parasitism are well-documented behaviors with direct observational evidence. The only material limitation is deciding which modern cuckoo taxon the text denotes.

assessments.operationalization: Compare peafowl age at first reproduction and observed or maximum lifespan with the stated three and twenty-five years.

candidate_datasets.name: AnAge: The Animal Ageing and Longevity Database
candidate_datasets.role: public longevity and life-history records for peafowl

obstacles: About twenty-five years could mean typical or maximum lifespan.
Captive and wild longevity differ.
assessments.rationale: Both variables are standard and public records exist. Longevity interpretation and captive bias prevent a fully clean resolution of the compound statement.

assessments.operationalization: Map the named groups to modern taxa and classify each by oviparity, ovoviviparity, or viviparity, checking the stated exception separately.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: public reproductive-mode records for fishes

obstacles: Cartilaginous genus and fishing-frog do not map cleanly to one coherent modern clade.
Reproductive modes vary within cartilaginous fishes.
assessments.rationale: Modern reproductive-mode data can decisively test mapped taxa. The ancient grouping and exception make the universal formulation only partially resolvable as stated.

assessments.operationalization: Identify the smooth shark taxon and determine from embryological anatomy whether embryos have a maternal attachment that transfers nutrients after yolk depletion.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: taxonomic and reproductive context for smooth-hound sharks

obstacles: Smooth shark is taxonomically ambiguous.
Detailed maternal nutrient-transfer anatomy is mainly in specialist papers.
assessments.rationale: The proposed mechanism has observable anatomical consequences. Public taxonomic data help, but specialist embryological evidence must be compiled and may cover only some candidate species.

assessments.operationalization: Across cartilaginous fish species, compare gestation lengths with six months and inspect pregnancies for simultaneous broods at distinct conception times.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: public life-history and reproduction records for sharks and rays

obstacles: Gestation is unknown for many species.
Superfoetation is difficult to distinguish from delayed development.
assessments.rationale: The duration bound is directly testable for species with records, while superfoetation needs stronger developmental evidence. Coverage is insufficient for the entire class.

assessments.operationalization: Classify reproductive mode for every living cetacean species and check for any egg-laying species.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: public mammal species accounts documenting live birth in cetaceans

assessments.rationale: Cetaceans map cleanly to a modern clade and reproductive mode is unambiguous. Existing public zoological data cover the clade sufficiently for a decisive test.

assessments.operationalization: For candidate dolphin species, compare gestation duration with ten months and test whether recorded births occur exclusively in summer at each population's latitude.

candidate_datasets.name: AnAge: The Animal Ageing and Longevity Database
candidate_datasets.role: public mammalian gestation records

obstacles: Dolphin denotes multiple species.
Birth season varies by species, population, and hemisphere.
assessments.rationale: Gestation can be checked readily for mapped species. The universal seasonal component is less adequately covered and requires geographically explicit birth records.

assessments.operationalization: For seal species plausibly intended, compare litter-size ranges, teat counts, and nursing observations with the stated values.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: public pinniped reproduction and anatomy accounts

obstacles: Seal is a broad vernacular category.
Teat-count data may not be tabulated across species.
assessments.rationale: Litter size and nursing are well documented, and anatomy is observable. The broad name and compound variables limit full-scope resolution.

assessments.operationalization: For externally spawning oviparous fishes, compare embryo development in eggs exposed and unexposed to milt.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: public reproductive-mode information for oviparous fishes

obstacles: The word most requires a defined taxonomic denominator.
assessments.rationale: External fertilization has a direct experimental criterion and extensive public documentation. The general mechanism can be tested cleanly with standard reproductive evidence.

assessments.operationalization: Count annual spawning bouts for mapped oviparous fishes and test whether one is modal, then test whether the black goby has two.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: public spawning-season and reproductive records

obstacles: Black goby mapping may be uncertain.
Multiple spawning within a season is incompletely recorded.
assessments.rationale: Spawning frequency is measurable and species records exist, but database coverage is uneven and repeated batches may not be consistently distinguished from seasons.

assessments.operationalization: Identify the sheat-fish and measure male guarding duration and egg predation during guarded spawning events.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: taxonomic and behavioral species information for sheat-fish

obstacles: Ancient sheat-fish requires taxonomic mapping.
Guarding duration is likely scattered in behavioral studies.
assessments.rationale: The behavior and duration provide a strong test, but no broad public behavioral table is evident. Existing species literature can resolve mapped populations only.

assessments.operationalization: Use eel life-cycle, larval, gonadal, and genetic evidence to test whether eels descend from adult eels through gametes rather than arising from mud organisms.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: public eel reproduction and life-cycle records

obstacles: Earth's guts is not a modern taxon, but the claimed origin has clear alternatives.
assessments.rationale: Although the proposed source is archaic, it predicts absence of ordinary eel reproduction and ancestry. Existing developmental and genetic evidence decisively discriminates spontaneous origin from reproduction.

assessments.operationalization: Define shoaling species and, by hemisphere and locality, estimate the proportion whose spawning peaks near the spring equinox.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: public spawning-season records for many fish species

obstacles: Shoaling is not a fixed taxonomic group.
Spawning phenology varies geographically and has uneven coverage.
assessments.rationale: The seasonal prediction is measurable once terms and latitude are specified. Existing records can test many species but not the broad scope uniformly.

assessments.operationalization: Compare offspring number per reproductive event between cartilaginous and other fishes, then model whether reproductive mode explains the difference after body size and phylogeny are controlled.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: public fecundity and reproductive-mode records

obstacles: The causal owing-to component is confounded by body size and evolutionary history.
Fecundity definitions differ between live-bearing and egg-laying fishes.
assessments.rationale: The fecundity association is accessible with existing data. Attributing it specifically to viviparity is harder and observational comparative analysis cannot eliminate all plausible confounding.

assessments.operationalization: Compare domestic pig gestation lengths and maximum litter sizes with four months and twenty piglets.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: public domestic pig life-history and reproduction information

obstacles: Breed and husbandry affect litter-size maxima.
assessments.rationale: Both variables are standard livestock measures with extensive public records. The numerical statements can be checked directly, including breed variation.

assessments.operationalization: Check sheep and goat gestation lengths, then model annual birth frequency against nutrition and solar or climatic conditions.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: public sheep and goat reproductive life-history information

obstacles: Comfort and well fed need proxies.
Management practices confound climate and birth frequency.
assessments.rationale: Five-month gestation is directly resolvable. The conditional claim about two births yearly requires interpreted exposures and is strongly confounded by husbandry.

assessments.operationalization: Map Laconian hounds to the nearest defensible modern population and compare gestation and eye-opening times with sixty and twelve days.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: general canine reproductive benchmarks

obstacles: The ancient Laconian hound has no certain modern breed mapping.
General dog data cannot establish a breed-specific claim.
assessments.rationale: The variables have abundant canine benchmarks, but the population named in the claim is historical and taxonomically unavailable. Only the general biological plausibility and proxy populations can be tested.

assessments.operationalization: Use cattle reproductive records to compare conception-to-calving duration and the frequency of singleton versus multiple births with the stated values.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: public cattle gestation and litter-size information

assessments.rationale: Gestation and litter size are routinely recorded for cattle at very large scale. The stated duration and usual singleton birth have direct, decisive criteria.

assessments.operationalization: Use horse breeding records to compare conception-to-foaling duration and singleton versus twin birth frequencies with the stated values.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: public horse gestation and litter-size information

assessments.rationale: These are standard, extensively recorded equine reproductive variables. Existing evidence can resolve both parts directly with minimal analysis.

assessments.operationalization: For each domestic camel species, compare gestation duration and observed maximum offspring per birth with ten months and one.

candidate_datasets.name: AnAge: The Animal Ageing and Longevity Database
candidate_datasets.role: public mammalian gestation and life-history records

obstacles: Camel may denote dromedary or Bactrian camel.
Rare twin births require very large records to assess never more.
assessments.rationale: The reproductive variables are standard and public data exist. Species ambiguity and the absolute upper-bound wording make complete resolution more demanding.

assessments.operationalization: From documented elephant births, record nursing anatomy, time to first supported and unsupported walking, and neonatal visual responsiveness.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: public elephant development and nursing accounts

obstacles: Immediately requires a time threshold.
Birth-event measurements are scattered across zoo and field reports.
assessments.rationale: All components are observable, but public structured data are unlikely to combine them or define immediacy consistently. Existing reports can resolve behavior for observed births, not necessarily the full scope.

assessments.operationalization: For deer species plausibly denoted by hind, compare gestation duration and litter-size distributions with eight months and predominantly one fawn.

candidate_datasets.name: AnAge: The Animal Ageing and Longevity Database
candidate_datasets.role: public deer gestation and life-history records

obstacles: Hind may refer to a particular deer species rather than all deer.
Gestation and twinning differ among deer species.
assessments.rationale: The numerical life-history traits are well represented in public resources. Taxonomic scope determines the answer, so the broad modern restatement cannot be fully resolved without mapping.

assessments.operationalization: Compare bear neonate-to-mother mass ratios with those of other mammals and code neonatal vision, pelage, locomotor development, and organ maturity.

candidate_datasets.name: AnAge: The Animal Ageing and Longevity Database
candidate_datasets.role: public mammalian body mass and life-history data

obstacles: Incompletely formed organs is not a standard variable.
The superlative requires comparable neonatal data across all animals.
assessments.rationale: Blindness and relative size can be tested for bears, but smoothness and inarticulate organs require interpretation. Existing data do not adequately support the universal smallest-relative-to-mother comparison.

assessments.operationalization: Use lion reproductive records to estimate breeding intervals, birth seasonality, modal litter size, and observed maximum litter size.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: public lion reproduction and life-history accounts

obstacles: Birth seasonality varies among populations.
assessments.rationale: Lion reproduction is extensively documented in public species accounts and long-term studies. Each numerical or seasonal component has a direct observational test.

assessments.operationalization: For hare species, estimate breeding season, detect overlapping pregnancies, and measure postpartum conception and interbirth intervals.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: public hare reproductive biology accounts

obstacles: Hares comprise multiple species and climates.
True superfoetation is difficult to distinguish from superfecundation or staggered development.
assessments.rationale: Year-round breeding and short postpartum intervals can be tested from existing life-history studies. The mechanism and broad taxonomic scope are less completely resolved.

assessments.operationalization: During field-mouse outbreaks, measure crop biomass immediately before and after single nights and test whether losses can approach the entire harvest.
obstacles: Nearly entire and overnight require unusually dense temporal measurements.
Field mouse and crop context are unspecified.
Existing loss estimates usually aggregate longer periods.
assessments.rationale: The event is measurable, but the extreme magnitude and one-night interval require high-frequency outbreak observations unlikely to exist as a public dataset. General rodent damage data would test only a weaker proxy.
